metaDescription: Six compact canister vacuums for dorms, small flats and closets, compared on weight, footprint, bag or bin size, cord length and how they store and carry.
expertTake: The Oreck Compact at about 5.5 lb is the best compact canister because it is the smallest and lightest here and carries a HEPA inner bag. The Eureka NEN110A is the value pick for a household that wants a bigger bagless bin in a light body. Anyone with a large home or deep carpet should skip compacts and choose a full-size canister.
introParagraphs: A compact canister earns its keep by fitting where a full-size machine will not: a dorm closet, a studio cupboard, a boat, a car boot or a flat with narrow stairs. The trade for the small footprint is a smaller bag or bin, a shorter hose and a lighter motor, and the question is which of those compromises suits the way you clean.

What matters is how small the machine really is, how well it carries and what it gives up. A light body that holds a tiny bag is annoying on a big floor, and a larger body with a bigger bin is a bad fit for a closet shelf. The six picks below cover the real range, with notes on each machine's limits.

products.name: Oreck Compact canister, 5.5 lb, 20 ft cord, HEPA inner bag

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: HEPA inner bag with AirClean filter, 99.95 percent

products.description:
The Oreck Compact is the smallest and lightest machine in the group at 5.5 lb, and it is built to be carried. A 20 ft power cord gives a whole-home reach from a few outlets, and the listing describes portable cleaning that is lightweight and effortless.

A HEPA inner bag combined with an AirClean filter is listed as capturing 99.95 percent of particles, which is unusual in a machine this small. That filtration, plus the bagged design, keeps dust inside when you change the bag. It is a plain machine for carpet and hard floors, with no powered head and a small bag.

A small bag packs quickly, so keep a spare in the cupboard and swap early. Wipe the hose cuff and check the filters on schedule. It is the machine for a dorm, a flat or a second home. A body this light can tip when you pull the hose sharply, so guide it with a steady, low tug rather than a yank. A small canister rewards a calm technique: let the head glide and let the hose follow.
products.bestFor: Small spaces and second homes that want the lightest, most portable canister.
pros: HEPA inner bag with AirClean filter
cons: No powered head for deep carpet

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL Pro 5 super compact canister, 5 lb, stretch hose

specList.label: Carry
specList.value: By hand or over the shoulder

products.description:
The XL Pro 5 is a commercial design that happens to be the lightest machine here at 5 lb. It can be carried by hand or over the shoulder, and a stretch hose adds reach for shelves and stairs without a rigid wand.

Because it is a commercial machine, the controls are plain and the parts are standard, which makes it a reliable choice for a small flat that gets daily use. The body is tiny, and so is the bag, which means frequent changes on a big job. Refinement and quiet are not on offer.

Carry it by the handle and let the hose do the work. Keep spare bags where you can find them. Compared with the household Oreck it is plainer and more repairable, with less filtration. If you have a tiny staircase, the five-pound body is easy to carry in one hand while the other holds the banister. A fabric cover on the shelf where it lives keeps dust off the body and the hose.
products.bestFor: Small flats that want a very light, repairable machine for daily use.
cons: Plain and louder than household machines

products.name: Hoover Commercial PortaPower compact canister, 8 lb, blower

specList.label: Carry
specList.value: By hand or over the shoulder

products.description:
The PortaPower is a compact canister at 8 lb with a built-in blower, a feature that makes it unusually flexible in a small space. You can vacuum the flat and then blow out a balcony, a car boot or a workshop corner.

A stretch hose adds reach, and the machine can be carried by hand or over the shoulder, which makes stairs easy. It has a commercial feel: plain, repairable and not quiet. The body is larger than the Oreck's, so it fits a cupboard but not a drawer.

Check the blower port is clean before use, and replace the bag at three quarters full. Someone wanting a compact machine with an extra job will find that here. The blower is useful for drying a sink, clearing a vent grille or tidying a garage floor, though you should not use it near fine powders indoors. Because it is a commercial design, spare bags and hoses are widely stocked.
products.bestFor: Small households that want a compact canister with a blower for outdoor spaces.

products.name: Eureka Whirlwind NEN110A bagless canister, 8.15 lb, 2.5L bin

specList.label: Running cost
specList.value: No bags or filters, per listing

products.description:
The NEN110A is the largest-bin compact at 2.5 liters, and it weighs 8.15 lb. For a small flat that has more floor than the tiny Orecks can handle in one go, the bigger bin means fewer stops.

It is bagless, and the listing says no bags or filters are required, which removes the running cost. A bagless body is easy to see into and quick to empty, though dust rises at the bin. The design is light and simple, with no powered head.

Empty the container after each use and wipe it dry. Check the hose for blockages. Think of it as the middle path between a tiny machine and a full-size canister. A clear container lets you spot a lost earring or a coin before it clogs the hose, which a bag would hide. If you share a flat, a bagless machine is also easy for everyone to empty without learning how to change a bag.
products.bestFor: Small homes that want a bigger bagless bin in a light body.
pros: No bags or filters per listing

products.name: Bissell Zing 2154A bagged canister, auto cord rewind, flip switch
products.description:
The Zing is a lightweight bagged canister with a button that rewinds the cord, which is the feature that makes a small machine easy to put away. A flip switch on the head moves between carpet and hard floor, and variable suction lets you lower the power for curtains and upholstery.

It is a little larger than the Orecks and has no powered head. The cord rewind alone is worth it for people who dislike winding, and the bag is a reasonable size for a flat. A mixed floor of rugs and bare boards is well within its range.

With a small bag, three quarters full arrives quickly, so keep the hose clear and a spare handy. If you have a tiny closet, check its footprint against your space before you buy. The cord rewind has a practical limit: it works best if you guide the plug in by hand, because a loose plug can whip and chip a wall. Wipe the cord with a dry cloth as it retracts, and it will stay clean and supple for years.
products.bestFor: Small flats with rugs and bare floors that value easy storage.

products.name: DUMOS bagless canister, 850W, 16kPa listed, 1.8L bin, washable HEPA

specList.label: Filter
specList.value: Washable HEPA, rinse and air dry

products.description:
The DUMOS is an import compact with a washable HEPA filter and a large 1.8 liter dust bin for its class. An 850 W motor with a listed 16 kPa and a one-click empty release make it easy to use, and the listing says you rinse the filter in clean water and air dry it.

The suction figure is a listing claim, with no shared test behind it. A washable HEPA filter is a convenience, and it also removes the cost of replacement filters, though a washed filter may not hold its rating as well as a sealed one. The brand is unfamiliar, so parts and support are uncertain.

Rinse the filter monthly and dry it fully. Keep the receipt and check the warranty. It suits a buyer who wants a bigger bin and a washable filter at a compact size. Make a note of the filter size and where to buy a spare, since a washable filter still wears out after a year or two of rinsing. If the bin latch feels loose when it arrives, return it, because a bin that falls off in use is a nuisance and a mess.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a washable HEPA filter and a big bin in a compact body.
cons: Listed kPa has no shared test

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Oreck Compact at 5.5 lb and the XL Pro 5 at 5 lb are the smallest here, while the Hoover at 8 lb and the Eureka at 8.15 lb are larger. A compact machine only helps if it fits your cupboard. Measure the space before you buy. Remember that the hose and wand need somewhere to live too, so a machine that fits the cupboard but leaves the hose dangling is a poor fit. Look for onboard clips that hold the wand and tools on the body.

A compact body means a small bag or bin. The DUMOS has a 1.8 liter bin and the Eureka 2.5 liters, while the Orecks use small bags. A small bag is fine for a studio and frustrating for a family flat. A rough rule is to change a small bag after every two or three rooms, not once a month. If that sounds like too much, pick a bagless model with a bigger bin, or step up to a full-size machine.

The Oreck Compact has a 20 ft cord, and the Bissell Zing has an automatic rewind. A short cord means more outlet changes, which is annoying in a big room. A stretch hose, as on the Hoover and the XL Pro 5, adds reach. Because a compact body is light, a short hose and a heavy wand can pull it over, so a balanced setup matters. Try pulling the hose around a corner and see whether the body follows or tips.

The Oreck Compact lists a HEPA inner bag with an AirClean filter at 99.95 percent, and the DUMOS a washable HEPA. Other compacts have basic filters. A small machine can still be a clean one. A HEPA bag only helps if the bag seals against the body, so check the collar and replace the bag when it is torn. For allergies, a compact machine is a supplement to, not a substitute for, a sealed full-size vacuum.

A 5 lb body is easy to lift onto a stair and carry between floors. Heavier compacts roll less well on rugs. Choose by how often you carry the machine. If the machine lives on one floor and is rolled, weight matters less than wheel quality and balance. If you carry it up and down every week, every pound counts, and a shoulder strap or a good handle is worth having.

Smaller motors, smaller bags and no powered head are the normal trade. A compact is a second machine or a small-home machine, not a deep cleaner for large carpets. Be honest about the size of your home. If you have more than about two rooms of carpet, a compact will feel like a chore, and a full-size canister will be a better buy. A compact shines as a second machine for the stairs, the car and the odd spill.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared published weights. The Oreck pair led at 5 and 5.5 lb. Lighter bodies scored higher for compacts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bags and bins, from the Orecks' small bags to the Eureka's 2.5 liters. Big bins in light bodies scored well.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We read for HEPA bags and washable HEPA. The Oreck Compact's HEPA inner bag led. Basic filters scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited cord rewind, stretch hoses and carrying options. The Bissell Zing and Hoover earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We read owner feedback patterns on bag size complaints, hose kinks and storage. Cost shaped the final sequence slightly, and no dollar figures are used.

cards.label: Bagged
cards.text: The Orecks, Hoover and Bissell contain dust at emptying. The bags are small and need replacing.

cards.label: Bagless
cards.text: The Eureka and DUMOS avoid bag costs and have bigger bins. They release dust when emptied.

howToChoose.note: Pick bagged for cleaner emptying, and bagless for bigger bins and no bags.

howToChoose.subheading: For Dorms and Small Flats Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a body that fits a closet, a bag or bin you can live with and a cord long enough for a room.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Oreck Compact and XL Pro 5 are smallest, with the Eureka as the bigger-bin choice.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more on the Oreck Compact if you value filtration and a tiny body. Small does not need to mean dirty.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save with the Eureka or Hoover if the flat is small and the floors are bare. A plain machine is enough.

maintenance.why: A small bag packs quickly and cuts airflow. Keep a spare set in the closet.
A small bin fills fast. Tip it into a bag held close.
A clogged filter cuts airflow. Dry any washed filter fully.
Compact hoses are narrow and clog easily. Clear them with a broom handle.
A tight wrap cracks the cable. Auto rewind avoids this.

faq.a: For small floors, yes. Smaller motors and bags limit them on large or deep-carpeted homes, and you will change bags more often. If your floor area is modest, the lower weight and easy storage outweigh the limits.

faq.q: How small is a compact canister?
faq.a: Between about 5 and 8 lb here, small enough for a closet shelf or a stair carry. Measure your space before you buy.

faq.q: Is bagged or bagless better for a compact?
faq.a: Bagged is cleaner to empty, but bags are small and need replacing. Bagless has a bigger bin and no bags, though dust rises when you empty it. Choose by whether dust or bag changes bother you more.
Some do. The Oreck Compact lists a HEPA inner bag and the DUMOS a washable HEPA filter.
Low-pile carpet and rugs, yes. Deep carpet needs a powered head, which compacts rarely have.

faq.q: Is a compact a good second vacuum?
faq.a: Yes. It handles stairs, cars and quick jobs while a bigger machine handles the main floors.
